note: With now() or transaction_timestamp() the second DELETE would still be refused, because the transaction began before the fence expired. SQLite has no in-statement sleep, so this runs on PostgreSQL only.

sqlite_check_sql: SELECT state || ',' || CASE WHEN terminal_at_unix_micro BETWEEN CAST(unixepoch('subsec') * 1000000 AS INTEGER) - 60000000 AND CAST(unixepoch('subsec') * 1000000 AS INTEGER) THEN 'true' ELSE 'false' END FROM hec_requests
note: Abandoned reservations carry no committed time, so the trigger stamps clock_timestamp() in microseconds. The bounds prove the unit and that the value comes from the database clock during the statement. PostgreSQL re-checks a foreign key on UPDATE of a row inserted earlier in the same transaction, so the seed includes the parents.
